A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DDIM-inversion research. All 20 pages of v2 and 32 pages of v3, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison. Retained material can be matched despite extensive relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original correlation, geometry, inversion-error, interpolation, editing and image-assignment experiments, plus model-training analyses in Appendix G.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical analyses and adds forward-diffusion intervention results, inversion-step sensitivity experiments, real-image editing examples and reconstruction failure cases.

M1.justification: v2 Section 5 replaces early inversion predictions with saved ground-truth denoising outputs. v3 Section 4 instead applies forward diffusion with fresh Gaussian noise before resuming DDIM inversion. This introduces a practical stochastic procedure that removes the requirement for saved sampling trajectories.

E1.justification: The core training datasets and generation domains remain unchanged. v3 Appendix K adds qualitative editing of ImageNet-R-TI2I images with IF, extending the generated-source-image evaluations in v2 to real input images.

E2.justification: Corresponding interpolation and editing comparisons retain Gaussian-noise generations and standard DDIM-inversion latents as controls. No additional named inversion competitor is evaluated; the expanded discussion of other inversion techniques does not establish baseline participation.

E3.justification: v3 adds masked-region PNG bits-per-pixel evaluation, a seven-setting correlation sweep from 10 to 1,000 inversion steps, and real-image editing that switches conditioning after 6% of denoising steps. Intervention evaluations now use forward diffusion and revised replacement fractions. The main 50/100-step settings and guidance scale of 1 remain.

E4.justification: v3 adds tests of correlation persistence at high step counts, plain-versus-non-plain compressibility, and the new intervention's replacement-fraction tradeoffs. Appendix N.1 demonstrates reconstruction failures at 10–20% replacement, while Appendix K adds stochastic editing case studies. Earlier triangle, mapping and training-time analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v2 Table 13 includes ± values for DreamSim, LPIPS and SSIM throughout the intervention sweep. v3 Table 13 reports only point estimates, including for retained controls, although ± reporting remains elsewhere. No increase in repeated experimental runs or new significance-testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Oracle-intervention results in v2 Tables 9 and 12–13 are replaced by forward-diffusion results in v3 Tables 7, 9 and 13. For example, one replaced DiT inversion step gives interpolation FID 19.70 in v2 and 16.89 in v3 under different procedures. New correlation and compressibility results are added; retained editing scores also change, and the IF assignment results from v2 Table 8 are omitted.

T1.justification: v3 Equation 5 introduces a piecewise mathematical definition combining forward diffusion and DDIM inversion at a selected cutoff. Existing DDPM/DDIM derivations, triangle-angle construction, masking definitions and normalized-error formulas are retained. No new theorem, proof or theoretical guarantee is supplied.

C1.justification: v2 primarily diagnoses inversion correlations and demonstrates mitigation using ground-truth predictions. v3 adds an explicit fourth contribution and corresponding abstract/conclusion claims: early forward diffusion decorrelates latents and improves editing and interpolation while preserving reconstruction quality. This adds a practical algorithmic contribution to the retained analytical claims.

C2.justification: v3 connects early inversion errors to trajectory curvature and noise-schedule singularities, and explains forward replacement through the chiefly denoising role of final generation steps. New limitations discuss weaker effects for CelebA-HQ LDM, dependence on inversion-step count, and reconstruction information lost through excessive replacement, supported by failure examples.

D1.justification: v3 adds pseudocode, hardware specifications, model-specific batch sizes and step timings, and an approximately 95 GPU-hour reproduction estimate. Appendix K documents GPT-4o annotation and real-image conditioning details. The code URL is unchanged. Algorithm 1's DDIM noise coefficient differs from Equation 5, leaving an implementation inconsistency.

R1.justification: v3 adds focused references concerning trajectory curvature and diffusion's generative versus denoising phases, and expands the Renoise and exact-inversion discussion. The noise-image and optimal-transport literature is retained in Appendix L. Wolberg's image-morphing survey is removed; duplicated DiffusionCLIP references do not represent additional research coverage.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: experimental details are condensed into Section 3, mapping discussion and experiments move into Appendix L, and the separate mitigation section becomes part of an integrated problem-and-solution Section 4. The abstract, contributions and conclusion are rewritten, and the appendices gain a contents page and revised organization.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the two-column format with a predominantly single-column layout using wrapped displays. Figure 6 is redesigned, Figure 7 changes from radar charts to grouped bars, and new sensitivity, editing, failure and interpolation displays appear. Figure 7's panel labelled LPIPS contains values matching Table 13's DreamSim entries.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the analysis more useful through an intervention requiring no saved ground truth, supported by interpolation results and real-image examples. Step-count sensitivity and explicit reconstruction failures also clarify applicability. These gains are tempered by inconsistent CLIP values between Tables 10 and 13, Figure 7's metric mislabelling, the Algorithm 1 versus Equation 5 mismatch, and reduced uncertainty reporting in the intervention sweep. Together, these support a limited net quality improvement.
